title: lora_l2: recv_async re-arm gives up after 3 EBUSY attempts and aborts the module
description: Found while debugging vn0t. After a single RX authentication failure in the ping_l2 loopback run, the RX thread logs 'recv_async arm failed (-16 EBUSY), retrying' 3 times (10ms apart) then 'giving up, deinit/init required' — leaving the module in ABORTED so every later TX returns -ENETDOWN and every stats read -ECANCELED until a full deinit/init cycle. A transient EBUSY (loopback TX/RX overlap arming the radio while busy) should not brick the radio: either retry with backoff for longer / indefinitely while the module is enabled, or re-arm lazily on the next TX completion. File under robustness; interacts with the -200 auth failure (vn0t follow-up) but is an independent state-machine defect.
close_reason: Fixed in cf9afa78a1 (on top of origin/main's lora_loopback which gained the upstream user_data param). Root cause: the loopback driver kept data->recv_cb registered ACROSS deliveries while the lichen RX layer re-arms after each processed packet (mandatory for real sx12xx radios where RX_DONE disarms) — every re-arm hit -EBUSY (driver rejects double-arm) and after 3 tries the RX layer set LORA_ABORTED, bricking the module until deinit/init. Fix: one-shot arming in rx_work — each delivery consumes the registration (recv_cb/cb_user_data cleared under rx_lock BEFORE invoking), gated on the registration being unchanged so a racing recv_async(NULL)/re-arm is never clobbered and a canceled callback never fires (canceled in-flight packet is dropped, matching post-disarm discard). Validated on heft: no arm-failure/abort logs remain, module stays up across all reinit cycles, suite 6/7. Reviews: pass 1 found the clear TOCTOU, pass 3 found the cancel-race/UAF variant — both closed by the gated clear (verification pass PASS); pass 2 (security) PASS. The remaining udp failure is a separate replay-rejection issue filed as a follow-up bead.
